discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave photons and dispersive qubit readout
motivation: The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in Josephson circuits. The next decisive step was circuit quantum electrodynamics. Blais, Schoelkopf and colleagues proposed coupling a superconducting qubit to an on-chip microwave resonator. In 2004 Wallraff, Schoelkopf and co-workers achieved strong coupling between a single artificial atom and a single photon. This brought cavity-QED physics into solid-state circuits and reached coupling strengths far beyond those possible with atoms. The architecture delivered quantum non-demolition dispersive readout, photon-mediated qubit-qubit gates and the transmon's protection against charge noise. It also enabled Fock-state and cat-state engineering and bosonic error-correcting codes. Today essentially every superconducting quantum processor measures and couples its qubits through circuit QED, including the recent demonstrations of error correction below threshold. It is both a new regime of light-matter physics and the enabling technology of a field.
